title: Global vehicle-fire data inventory
scope: Structured follow-up to the 195-country screening in country-screening.json. This is a source inventory, not a claim that every national authority, insurer, fire service, police force, or roadside-assistance operator worldwide was individually audited.

classification.core_comparable: Fire numerator and vehicle exposure are both available for at least two powertrain groups within a defined population and period, with enough matching definitions to calculate or review a rate.
classification.supporting: Useful official or primary fire counts, grouped rates, battery-involvement information, or denominators, but missing at least one condition needed for a comparable three-group rate.
classification.context_only: Useful for scope, calibration, risks, or leads; not suitable as a fire-incidence rate.

records.sourceType: Official fire-service incident extraction and official fleet statistics (BIL54)
records.fireMetric: Fire-service dispatches to fires involving electric and hybrid cars combined, compared with other cars; dispatches, not necessarily unique vehicles.
records.exposureMetric: Registered vehicle stocks; rates reported by BRS per 10,000 vehicles.
records.quality: High for Denmark's combined-group comparison; cannot distinguish BEV from HEV/PHEV. Numerator is dispatch count and denominator stock rather than vehicle-kilometres; check factsheet details before re-computing. Older 2024 factsheet says cross-country comparisons differ because Sweden/Norway do not include vehicle fires spreading to buildings in the same way.
records.use: Supporting incidence; strong evidence that Denmark's combined alternative-drive group had lower recorded dispatch rates than other cars in 2024-25. Not a direct input for separate BEV/hybrid rates.

records.publisher: Thatcham Research; figures repeated by UK Department for Transport in a Parliamentary written answer
records.sourceType: Insurance register claims compared with fleet numbers; underlying full analysis is not publicly reproduced
records.period: Thatcham analysis cited as 2022; parliamentary answer 2026-03-09
records.fireMetric: Annual vehicle-fire claims / vehicles of each powertrain on UK roads, according to the DfT answer summarising Thatcham Research.
records.exposureMetric: Road fleet by powertrain; exact periodization and adjustment not published in the answer.
records.quality: Very relevant independent supporting evidence, but the small MIAFTR BEV claim count was explicitly described by Thatcham as very small; exact count, confidence intervals, annual exposure, and full methods are not public. The larger Thatcham report says EV fire claims were less common than petrol/diesel even after age was considered, but older EVs had greater uncertainty.
records.use: Supporting incidence; retain as a separate UK insurance estimate and never pool with dispatch counts without full method and coverage details. Strongly contradicts viral claims that hybrids necessarily have the highest fire rate.

records.publisher: Highway Loss Data Institute (HLDI), based on insurer submissions; report prepared for NHTSA
records.sourceType: Insurance claims with insured vehicle-year exposures
records.period: Model years 2014-2016; report December 2016; >39.6 million insured vehicle-years, >5,100 claims
records.fireMetric: Comprehensive insurance fire claims for non-crash, non-vandalism fire damage, by make/series; reported as relative frequencies, with some series and hybrid examples and claim counts.
records.exposureMetric: Insured vehicle years; claim-frequency denominator is explicit.
powertrains: individual model series; some hybrid series
records.quality: High quality denominator and insurer record; dated and restricted to insured US vehicle population and non-crash/non-vandalism fires. Does not offer harmonized powertrain totals or a full BEV/HEV/ICE comparison. Report requires vehicles to meet exposure/claim thresholds for individual series.
records.use: Supporting; possible robustness context and model-age effects, not a global rate input.

records.sourceType: Insurance fire claims per insured vehicle-year
records.period: 2021 bulletin, using later exposure period than 2018 exploration
records.fireMetric: Non-crash EV fire claims; historical exploratory sample
records.quality: Small number of claims; authors did not report regression due to sparse data. Prior study found a higher frequency for newer EVs, while the later data did not preserve that difference as vehicles aged. HLDI cautions that data may never be conclusive for this outcome.
records.use: Supporting only; key lesson that vehicle age and cause scope can change apparent rates.

records.publisher: Myndigheten för samhällsskydd och beredskap (MSB; now MCF), official report MSB1647
records.sourceType: National rescue-service incident review, free-text search, plus official fleet stock table
records.fireMetric: Incidents involving electric and electric/hybrid cars; arson excluded from this selected dataset. 40 electric/hybrid vehicles involved in fires in 2024; 23 in 2022 and 38 in 2023.
records.exposureMetric: End-2024 stock table: BEV 358,260; electric/plug-in hybrids 522,698; other fuels 4,096,833; total 4,977,791 passenger cars.
records.quality: Useful but incomplete: report says data are limited in quality/coverage and selected via free-text terms; arson is excluded from alternative-vehicle review. It separately says total car fires in 2024 were >3,100 including arson, so that all-fires figure is not directly comparable to the 40. Fleet table is point-in-time end-year stock, not annual vehicle-years. Do not compute a direct rate from unlike numerator scopes.
records.use: Supporting alternative-fire counts and high-quality stock denominator; potentially recover comparable rates only after matching event definition and excluding arson for all powertrains.

records.sourceType: National fire-brigade attendance register and case review
records.fireMetric: 254 fires attended by fire brigade involving 264 alternative-fuel vehicles; 42.4% full electric, 56.8% (plug-in) hybrid; battery burned in 18.7% of 262 battery-equipped vehicles. Separate accident counts: 176 accidents, 185 vehicles; 7 accident fires.
records.exposureMetric: No matched fleet denominator on report page.
records.quality: Excellent detail on event definitions, count of incidents vs count of vehicles, battery involvement, and charging status, but no ICE control group or exposure denominator; AAV includes more than road passenger cars.
records.use: Supporting numerator/hazard classification and de-duplication rules only; do not use as incidence rate.

records.publisher: London Fire Brigade, FOI response 7964.1; hosted by LFB
records.sourceType: Local fire brigade incident management data via FOI
records.fireMetric: 7,310 total vehicle-fire incidents, by recorded powertrain and year; includes car, bus, HGV, van and other road vehicles. In 2023: 71 electric-battery, 35 petrol/electric hybrid, 26 diesel/electric hybrid, 516 petrol, 288 diesel/biodiesel, 121 unknown. Fuel power types were not recorded for many events in 2019-2021; 4,570 events over 2019-23 have no fuel type recorded.
records.exposureMetric: No matching registered/insured vehicle-year denominators in the FOI response.
records.quality: Strong local numerator with incident detail and clear unknownness; 2021 onward reporting transition makes missing powertrain data substantial and early year comparison unreliable. Includes multiple vehicle classes and causes, including arson and fire spread.
records.use: Supporting incident counts and data-quality proof; pair only with matching London fleet-by-fuel and vehicle-class exposure if obtainable.

records.publisher: Home Office / Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (fire incident statistics)
records.period: Annual FIRE0302 tables; through 2024-25 in latest published series
records.fireMetric: Primary fires, fatalities and casualties in road vehicles by motive and vehicle type; national counts, not powertrain-specific.
records.exposureMetric: No vehicle energy-source field in standard reported tables; UK Parliament confirms fire-service collection does not identify whether involved vehicle was electric.
records.quality: Strong total fire numerator source, but no powertrain field means not a direct fire-rate source.
records.use: Context and total-fire calibration; not for BEV/hybrid/ICE comparisons.

records.sourceType: Insurance claim data synthesis, including confidential MIAFTR analysis
records.fireMetric: Full MIAFTR fire analysis is not published, but report documents that claim counts for EVs were very small, EV fires were less common than petrol/diesel even after age adjustment, and certainty for EVs older than five years was limited.
records.exposureMetric: Powertrain vehicle parc / exposure used internally; exact values omitted.
records.quality: Source is primary industry research and funded report, but underlying rate table and reproducible methods are withheld; suitable as supporting qualitative finding, not as a fully reproducible numerical source.
records.use: Supports age adjustment and low-count uncertainty; use the parliamentary rates separately as attributed figures.

records.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
records.sourceType: Multi-source statistical estimation of lithium-ion battery fires
records.period: EV and plug-in hybrid fires since 2011; publication 2026-03-10
records.fireMetric: Estimated 5,718 EV and plug-in hybrid fires since 2011, 95% interval 2,866-10,846; separate estimate of 198,000 LIB fires in structures.
records.exposureMetric: No matched vehicle-years by powertrain in this summary.
records.quality: Institutional estimation and uncertainty interval; period is cumulative and detection/data integration is model-based. Does not provide an annual per-fleet incidence rate or ICE comparison.
records.use: Context and possible numerator-reconstruction lead only.

records.publisher: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways / Press Information Bureau; eDAR crash data
records.fireMetric: 26 fire-involved EV accidents among 23,865 EV accidents reported in eDAR (8/5,594 in 2023; 9/7,817 in 2024; 9/10,454 in 2025).
records.exposureMetric: EV crash records only, not registered fleet or vehicle-years.
records.quality: Official but restricted to reported road accidents; excludes parked/non-crash fires and has no ICE fire comparator in this reported statistic.
records.use: Crash-conditioned fire proportion only; not annual vehicle-fire incidence.

records.publisher: Statistics Canada, National Fire Information Database
records.exposureMetric: Partial reporting from seven jurisdictions: NS, NB, Ontario, Manitoba, BC, Yukon, and Canadian Armed Forces; no powertrain-specific denominator in chart.
records.quality: Official partial-coverage national database; not all Canadian jurisdictions, and chart is not drivetrain-specific.
records.use: Regional total-fire baseline and a follow-up lead for provincial incident records; not a national per-powertrain rate.

records.sourceType: Official risk/implementation plan with fleet-stock table
records.fireMetric: Document is emergency-response risk plan; no harmonized annual fire numerator by powertrain in the surfaced table.
records.exposureMetric: Registered/licensed fleet: ICE 3,480,432; BEV 46,014; PHEV 17,711; other vehicles with some electric composition (including hybrids and fuel-cell vehicles) 156,673; total 3,700,861.
records.quality: Official denominator source and categorization; broad vehicle classes include light and heavy vehicles. No matched powertrain-specific fire counts in the report's fleet table.
records.use: Exposure denominator candidate only; must align vehicle class and acquire corresponding numerator.

records.sourceType: Official Information Act response from fire-service incident database
records.fireMetric: OIA response supplies total mobile-property/vehicle-fire counts; request/response is not reported by vehicle powertrain in the surfaced document.
records.quality: Official but total counts alone; incident-report public feed explicitly warns that it is not complete statistical data and should not be used for statistical analysis.
records.use: Follow-up lead for a targeted OIA request asking for incident count by vehicle class, fuel type, cause, and year; current response is context only.

records.publisher: U.S. Fire Administration / National Fire Protection Association estimate
records.sourceType: National estimated total fire count; NFIRS-based and statistical estimation
records.fireMetric: NFPA estimate of 211,500 vehicle fires in 2024; USFA notes unknowns are apportioned in relevant published tables.
records.exposureMetric: No powertrain-separated exposure in this statistic.
records.quality: Useful total scale, but estimated rather than raw census and no drivetrain breakout.
records.use: Context calibration only; must not be treated as fire count split by powertrain.

records.publisher: Ministry of Emergency Management fire and rescue sources as reported in public statistics
records.fireMetric: Reported 97,000 transport means fires; category broader than passenger cars and no powertrain split.
records.quality: Important size-of-country source but category and numerator scope too broad for direct passenger-car rate.
records.use: Lead for Ministry/fire-service microdata and fuel type tables; current figure context only.

highPriorityFollowups: Request Thatcham's MIAFTR 2022 fire numerator, matched exposure by fuel type, age adjustment, uncertainty and arson/third-party-fire scope.
Download and inspect BRS 2025 factsheet and underlying ODIN/BIL54 definitions; establish whether rates use year-end registrations or a within-year exposure average and how dispatches map to vehicles.
Request additional London Fire Brigade years through 2025/26 and matched vehicle parc by powertrain, using car-only events and explicit treatment of unknown fuel, spread and arson.
For Sweden, reconcile the MSB selected non-arson event set to all-powertrain counts under the same incident definition before calculating rates; preserve end-year vehicle fuel stocks.
For Netherlands, obtain Dutch registered-vehicle stocks by exact AAV fuel categories and passenger/commercial class; then evaluate an AAV rate, not a false BEV-vs-ICE comparison.
For New Zealand and Canada, ask national fire services/statistical agencies for annual vehicle-fire incident counts by vehicle class, fuel, cause, incident-vs-vehicle unit, and missing fuel rate.
Extend original-language searches for China, South Korea, Japan, Australia, Brazil, India, and major European markets, prioritizing paired fire numerator plus same-year fleet stock sources.
